subject: Private connectivity kickoff / governance alignment — Picarus Health
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@picarushealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@picarushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment kickoff: governance & connectivity questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the overview last week. We're ready to start the private deployment planning for Picarus Health (prod workloads) and want to lock down networking and governance items before the calendar kickoff. A few constraints from our side to surface up front:

- We run strict outbound firewall rules; only specific CIDRs and ports are permitted.
- We prefer connection patterns that minimize cross-account route changes; AWS PrivateLink would be ideal for the control plane if supported.
- On-prem package needs to support our HSM proxy (Yubikey-backed HSM) and run inside an isolated subnet with no public IPs.
- We'll need an audit trail for token usage and request logs for SOC review.

I've attached our initial VPC/network requirements and an install manifest for the on-prem appliance. Rajesh (cc'd) is our network lead — he'll be the day-to-day contact for peering and firewall work. Can Redwood confirm whether PrivateLink + VPC peering hybrid is supported, or if you recommend one approach over the other?

Proposed kickoff window: Wed 4/4 or Thu 4/5, mornings PST.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Cloud Operations
Picarus Health
Attachments: picarus-vpc-requirements.pdf, onprem-install-manifest.xlsx

Hi Samira — really appreciate the background and the manifests.

We can definitely support a hybrid model; I captured a quick agenda and attached our kickoff agenda so we have alignment before the meeting. High-level agenda:

1) Introductions & success criteria (CS + network)
2) Network inventory (CIDRs, NAT/GW, firewall rules)
3) Connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway)
4) Private endpoints & TLS/mTLS flows (HSM proxy requirements)
5) On-prem package timeline and runbook handoff
6) Security evidence needs & SOC2 artifacts
7) Action items / owners / dates

Proposed times: Wed 4/4 10:00am PT, Wed 4/4 3:30pm PT, Thu 4/5 9:00am PT — pick what works for your team and I will book.

cc @monica_patel to own success criteria and rollout plan, and @vivek_kulkarni to own the technical design.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-private-kickoff-agenda.md

From: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@picarushealth.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@picarushealth.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: helpdesk@picarushealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2028 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff: governance & connectivity questions

Thanks — a few quick technical notes from my side before the call:

- Current egress policy: only allow outbound to whitelisted CIDRs on ports 443, 22 (for admin), and 123 (NTP). We are reluctant to open broad ranges.
- Preferred CIDR for the Redwood-hosted VPC to peer with: 10.240.96.0/20 (we can adopt a /24 within that if needed).
- For data exfiltration control we prefer PrivateLink where possible, but our data plane patterns (large streaming payloads from on-prem edge to hosted GPU pools) make pure PrivateLink less efficient in our benchmarking.
- Attached is the onprem-install-manifest with node specs and an internal network diagram.

Two asks for the kickoff:
1) Can Redwood enumerate exactly which ports/outbound destinations the on-prem appliance will need to reach?
2) If we choose Peering + NAT, what are the recommended source IPs and port ranges for KV cache and token refresh?

-Rajesh
Network Lead, Picarus Health
Attachments: onprem-install-manifest.xlsx

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@picarushealth.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff: governance & connectivity questions

Hi Rajesh / Samira — quick technical recommendation based on the constraints you shared. TL;DR: hybrid PrivateLink (control plane) + VPC peering (data lane) gives the best tradeoff for throughput + minimal route changes.

Details / checklist:
- Control plane (auth, management): use AWS PrivateLink endpoints into a dedicated Redwood control VPC. This minimizes cross-account route edits and is compatible with strict egress rules.
- Data plane (payload, streaming tokens): VPC peering is more efficient for sustained high-throughput streaming; peer a dedicated data VPC with a /24 inside your 10.240.96.0/20.
- Ports: 443 (TLS) for control plane, 10250 and 22100-22110 TCP for high-volume streaming (these are the Redwood data ports for agent ingest / batching). We can compress ranges if your firewall requires.
- KV cache & token endpoints: token refresh to auth.redwood.ai:443, cache sync to cache.redwood.ai:443. No UDP required except NTP to 123.
- TLS: require mutual TLS between on-prem agent and Redwood gateway. We'll provide client certs signed by Redwood CA and rotate on 90d cadence.
- HSM: we recommend an HSM-proxy inside your VPC that the on-prem agent talks to over localhost; the proxy can then call out over TLS to Redwood key-escrow endpoints. If Yubikey-backed HSM is required on-prem, we can validate during the preflight.

Preflight checklist (to confirm before SOW sign-off):
- Confirm exact CIDR allocated for data VPC (/24)
- Open 443 and (10250, 22100-22110) to Redwood egress list or PrivateLink
- Provide a bastion/admin IP (or range) for initial debugging (we can lock down after validation)
- Share ASN if you want BGP-like routing (optional)

I've attached a quick network sketch. On the kickoff call I can walk through packet flows and NAT behavior.

— Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: network-diagram.png

Hi all — adding a couple of operational notes from infra/eng:

- On-prem package ETA: we can prepare a release candidate for your environment in 3 weeks following sign-off on the preflight checklist. Production release (GA) after a short staging validation (2–3 weeks).
- We will need a scoped SOW that captures the peering architecture, PrivateLink endpoints, testing windows, and rollback criteria. Can Tessa/Monica own generation of that SOW?
- Security review: please provide a list of required SOC2 artifacts; we will surface our SOC2 Type II report and network segmentation docs. See internal security link: https://drive.redwood.ai/security/soc2 (we'll share direct access with your security reviewers).

Goal: schedule the first validation window within two business weeks of the kickoff call.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
